title: Granular channel scheduling and policy sandbox (WIP)
content:
Objective:
Short-term prototype for a compact policy sandbox UI that lets users: configure notification channels, attach schedules/quiet windows per-channel, and preview effective policy for an SLO/alert. Focus is console surface for fast iteration (small screens, no full-page modal).

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Current alerting flows force a separate channel config page and a separate routing/policy composer; users have trouble understanding what the resulting fanout will be for a given alert (esp. with multiple schedules and fallbacks).
- Ops teams want per-channel quiet windows (e.g., paging only during business hours) and a way to simulate policy evaluation for a single alert instance before saving.
- PM/Support feedback: users create duplicate channels because they can’t tweak schedule/policy combinations easily.

High-level design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Compact: everything fits in an inspect pane (right rail) without navigating away from the alert rule list.
- Composable: channels, schedules, and transforms are small reusable blocks.
- Preview-first: immediate deterministic preview of final fanout for a sample incident.
- Safe-by-default: changes to schedule/policy require explicit canary toggle for production rules.

Wireframe notes (right-rail sandbox, mobile-compact):
- Top: rule selector (dropdown) + sample incident toggle (choose last 24h incident or fabricated example).
- Mid: list of notification rows (channel chip, priority selector, schedule pill, transform summary). Rows are draggable to reorder fallbacks.
- Each row expands inline to show schedule editor (day/time ranges + tz), overrides (silent for N minutes), and escalation actions.
- Bottom: live preview pane showing which endpoints would receive notifications for the selected sample incident and why (with color-coded reasons: "rule match", "out-of-hours", "fallback hit").
- Save bar: Save changes, Save as draft, Revert to production. Changes marked with yellow stripe until published.

Mini-component spec (for handoff):
- Channel chip: icon (email/slack/pager), display name, small kebab menu (edit channel, duplicate, delete). Click opens channel details in modal.
- Schedule pill: "Always" | "Weekdays 09:00-17:00 PST" | custom. Clicking opens inline editor.
- Priority selector: dropdown (page/immediate/notify-low). Priority drives alert aggregation and paging policy.
- Transform summary: one-line (e.g., "strip debug lines, include run_id"). Expand shows basic rules.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can attach multiple channels to a rule and set a schedule per channel.
- Live preview accurately reflects sample incident and shows why a channel would/ would not receive a notification.
- UI supports reordering channels to control fallback order.
- Changes are staged until explicitly published (clear visual state).

Edge cases/known unknowns:
- Timezones: users may expect schedule to follow rule timezone, channel timezone, or incident timezone. Default to rule timezone but provide clear label. Need UX copy.
- Overlapping schedules: precedence rules required (more restrictive wins?). Suggest: explicit deny > allow; but review with legal/ops.
- Large team channels (email distribution lists): preview should hide personal emails, show only channel names.
- Integration with Dedicated/Private: some channels (e.g., on-prem pager gateway) may be unavailable for hosted rules; show compatibility hints.

Backlog grooming items (rough priority):
- 1: Inline schedule editor component (design + small state machine for repeats).
- 2: Live preview engine endpoint (backend: simulate policy evaluation for a given sample incident).
- 3: Channel kebab actions (open channel modal, duplicate with schedule).
- 4: Canaries + staging: wire up staged changes with audit log entries.
- 5: Accessibility pass (aria labels for drag handles, keyboard reorder).
- 6: Mobile responsiveness tweaks (collapse preview into expandable section).

Implementation notes (infra & backend):
- Preview should be powered by a lightweight simulation API that takes: rule id, list of staged changes, sample incident payload -> returns list of channel outcomes with reasons. Cache simulations for 2 minutes per user to limit load.
- Schedules stored as RFC5545-ish recurrence simplified: days + time ranges + tz. Keep format compact for client.
- Rollout plan: behind feature flag for 20% of orgs, target customers who reported duplicate channels.

Handoff checklist for design -> eng sprint 1:
- Finalize inline schedule ux + copy (owner: Lena).
- Provide component library tokens for channel chip (owner: Devex).
- Contract spec for preview API (owner: Marco) + minimal sample payloads.
- Acceptance test matrix and 3 manual test cases (out-of-hours, fallback ordering, schedule override).

Unresolved questions (calls for async decisions):
- Should schedule precedence allow "exceptions" (e.g., schedule = business hours except specific dates)? If yes, we need holiday calendar integration.
- Do we allow per-channel dedup windows (suppress repeat notifications for N minutes) or just global rule-level suppression?
- Audit trail: do staged & published changes map to the same audit event type or separate events?

Quick user scenarios (to guide copy & microcopy):
1) On-call manager wants paging only during 09:00–18:00 Mon–Fri for a particular PagerDuty integration. They add channel, set schedule pill to Weekdays, set priority=page, preview shows no paging for sample incident on Saturday.
2) SRE wants Slack notifications always but wants to avoid duplicate pings: they set channel transform to attach alert_summary and set rule dedup to 5m; preview shows Slack once with summary.
3) Customer success needs email to always get notifications but not pages; set priority=notify-low, schedule=Always. Preview shows email delivered and no page.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus review on "preview" semantics and the save/publish model. We need to ensure users can't accidentally publish sweeping changes across many rules.
- UX copy suggestions inline: use explicit labels like "Staged changes" + "Publish to production".

Next steps / meetings:
- Sync w/ backend (Marco) 2025-01-22: define simulation API contract.
- Design review (Lena + Devex) 2025-01-27: finalize inline editor.
- Legal/security quick check 2025-01-30: schedule persistence + PII in previews.

Rough timeline (2-week iterations):
- Sprint A (2 weeks): inline schedule editor + channel chip + basic preview UI (no backend sim, use client-side heuristic).
- Sprint B (2 weeks): preview API + staging model + reorder persistence.
- Sprint C (2 weeks): QA, accessibility, rollout to feature flag, customer pilot.

Attachment ideas for next iteration:
- Compact SVG wireframe assets (right rail collapsed/expanded).
- Sample incident payloads for common Redwood alert types (latency spike, model OOM, inference errors).

Loose copy snippets (for UI):
- "Staged changes: these edits are not live until published"
- "Preview shows which channels would receive this alert and why"
- "Schedule applies to this channel only"
- "Reorder channels to change escalation order"

——
Working doc; please comment inline or add GH issue if you take an action.
